# Decisions: architecture-map

- 2026-08-08T18:02:41.124Z — rule: **Every module added under packages/*/src must get a line in docs/ARCHITECTURE.md in the same change — the suite fails until it does, and that failure is the cheapest moment to write it.** — chose **docs/ARCHITECTURE.md names EVERY module in packages/*/src, and test/architecture-doc.test.ts fails with the module's name when one is added without a line in the doc. The visual artifact is derived from the doc, never authored separately.** over a hand-maintained architecture doc kept honest by discipline, a generated-from-code doc, and publishing only the visual map because An architecture document in a codebase moving at this pace is a liability the moment it stops being true, because it will be BELIEVED after it stops being true — by a new contributor, by a future session reading it as orientation, by whoever renders it as a diagram. Prose rots silently; nobody notices a paragraph that no longer describes anything. Discipline was rejected because it is the same bet that already failed today: record-index's Phase 3 lagged its own design within hours of the design being made. Full generation from code was rejected because the valuable half of this doc is WHY each module exists and what it is not allowed to do, and no generator can derive that from source. So the split is: prose written by hand, completeness enforced mechanically. The test checks NAMING, not correctness — nothing mechanical can tell whether the sentence beside a module is still true — and that honest limit is still the difference between a doc that is incomplete and one that is silently wrong about what exists. Mutation-checked at introduction: adding an unnamed module fails the suite, removing it passes.
